A New Perspective on a Familiar Story

Audiences approaching the documentary You Can See Everything—co-directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim—typically arrive with pre-existing awareness of its central subject, Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes. Holmes, who is currently serving a prison sentence for defrauding investors, has been the subject of extensive media coverage, including the Hulu miniseries The Dropout, where she was portrayed by Amanda Seyfried.

While Fielder is widely recognized for his work on Nathan for You and The Rehearsal, the documentary introduces a less expected central figure in its second half: Billy Evans, Holmes's partner. Although Evans is not featured in the film's initial promotional campaign, his prominent screen time makes the project function effectively as a four-character drama alongside Holmes, Fielder, and an unannounced A-list cameo.

The Portrayal of Billy Evans

The documentary captures several unusual interactions involving Evans. Among the moments highlighted in the film are Evans demanding a percentage of the documentary's profits, expressing discomfort with questioning while appearing fully nude on camera, and intervening in domestic tasks such as cooking.

Following a two-year time jump in the film, the documentary depicts Evans exerting increased involvement in managing aspects of Holmes's public presence, including her social media accounts and an AI-generated likeness of her. The film also shows him engaging with media at double speed and visiting a shooting range, details that contribute to his depiction within the narrative.

Practical Implications and Context

For readers examining the documentary's place in current media, several distinctions should be noted:

  • Confirmed Elements: The documentary is co-directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim. It features Elizabeth Holmes and her partner Billy Evans, documenting interactions such as profit-participation requests and social media management following Holmes's conviction.
  • Unknowns and Uncertainties: The film leaves open questions regarding the extent of Holmes's awareness of Evans's financial demands and the precise motivations behind various interactions captured on camera. Viewers are left to interpret whether Holmes's responses stem from genuine belief or calculated evasion.
  • How to Verify: Readers interested in the original reporting and critical analysis can review the full review and context published in [The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/oct/22/you-can-see-everything-elizabeth-holmes-billy-evans-villain).
